interpretation: Linear PH baseline: Cox/Fine-Gray-style models are expected to remain competitive; RSF/GBSA need not improve.
Lower event-rate linear PH setting: simple structured models should remain stable if calibration is adequate.
Higher event-rate linear PH setting: absolute-risk error and calibration should be checked alongside ranking.
Nonlinear/interaction setting: RSF or GBSA may become more competitive if the nonlinear signal is strong enough.
Non-PH setting: flexible models may improve ranking, but absolute-risk calibration must be interpreted separately.
MAR missingness setting: high-dimensional models may become less stable if missingness interacts with weak signals.
High-dimensional sparse MRI setting: all-safe RSF/GBSA or penalised Cox-style models may have an advantage.
Strong competing-death setting: Fine-Gray and CIF-reconstruction models should be compared against individualised Cox CIF and AJ-null baselines.
